problem: Depth-based and generated-image visual locomotion policies are limited to low-level control because standard simulators lack real-world visual fidelity and complex geometry. Existing 3DGS/NeRF real-to-sim works focus on photorealism with limited physical interaction and no exploration ability for legged robots.
motivation: Real-world RL is unsafe and inefficient, while simulators leave a visual sim-to-real gap that blocks RGB-based ego-centric navigation. Reconstructing digital twins from casual RGB photos that are both photorealistic (3DGS) and physically interactive (mesh) allows training high-level visual policies that transfer zero-shot.
key_idea: Reconstruct real scenes from RGB images into a GS-mesh hybrid digital twin in Isaac Sim (3DGS for ego-view rendering, TSDF mesh for physics) with occlusion-aware object composition and randomization, then train an RGB-only hierarchical RL policy for zero-shot real quadruped deployment.
insight: Decoupling appearance (GS rendering) from physics (cropped mesh of central terrain) avoids the texture and bulge artifacts of textured-mesh rendering (PSNR 29.73 vs 27.73; real SR 20/6.67/0% vs 100/93.33/100%). Retaining scene-specific background (vs ImageNet random backgrounds, SR 43.33% in sim) and domain randomization matter (w/o DR real SR 53.33/6.67/0), and a ViT encoder beats a CNN encoder. RL exploration in the twin beats imitation learning from 60 real trajectories (0% real SR).
method: Geometry-consistent GS reconstruction: PGSR-style planar 3DGS with flattened Gaussians, Depth-Anything-V2 depth prior scale-aligned to SfM points by linear regression, monocular normal prior, and multi-view NCC loss
GS-mesh hybrid representation: 3DGS renders ego-view observations; TSDF fusion of rendered depth gives a mesh for collision and physics in Isaac Sim; camera intrinsics calibrated

Coordinate alignment: four-point registration of COLMAP frame to Isaac Sim via a regular reference block; Gaussian means, scales, rotations and SH coefficients (Wigner D-matrix) transformed accordingly

Occlusion-aware composition and randomization: objects (cones) reconstructed separately, cropped by mesh bounding boxes and merged into env Gaussians per episode with random positions; joint alpha-blending/z-buffering gives correct occlusion

Hierarchical RL: low-level LSTM+MLP locomotion policy (50 Hz, velocity commands to joint positions) frozen; high-level PPO policy at 5 Hz takes frozen ViT-tiny features, RGB color command, last action, proprioception; asymmetric critic; goal-distance/height/heading rewards
Domain randomization: camera pose noise, color/blur/noise image augmentation, 0-1 step image delay

setting.backbone: Frozen ViT-tiny (vit_tiny_patch16_224) encoder + LSTM+MLP actor-critic high-level policy (PPO) + LSTM+MLP low-level locomotion policy, trained from scratch
setting.model_size: ViT-tiny (~5M) encoder; policy sizes not given
setting.training_data: Simulated RL in 6 reconstructed indoor scenes from iPad/iPhone photos; low-level policy 80k iterations with 4096 agents; high-level 8k iterations with 64 agents; ~3 days on one 4090D
setting.observation: Monocular ego-view RGB (320x180 Insta360 Ace) + proprioception + RGB target-color command
setting.action_space: High-level velocity commands (Vx, Vy, Vyaw) at 5 Hz to low-level joint-position policy at 50 Hz
setting.privileged: none at test time (asymmetric critic uses privileged info only in training)

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 cone position sets x easy/medium/hard, 5 trials each; 15 s limit
numbers.backbone: ViT-tiny + LSTM/MLP RL policy, Unitree Go2
numbers.extra: zero-shot sim-to-real; success = contact with cone

numbers_note: Real-world results are split by difficulty (Easy/Medium/Hard) in Table I; the benchmark is the paper's own task, not a standard one.
results: On the paper's own cone-reaching task, the policy reaches 100/93.33/100% real SR (easy/medium/hard) with 4.96/6.28/9.09 s reaching time, versus SARO 66.67/26.67/0%, CNN encoder 73.33/66.67/6.67%, and IL 0%. In simulation it reaches 100% SR vs 43.33% for Random Background and 8.67% for IL.
limitations: Only static indoor scenes; a policy must be trained from scratch per task, taking ~3 days
RGB-only meshes have structural imperfections and need manual post-processing (manual alignment and bbox editing)
Evaluation is a single simple task (colored cone reaching) mostly in one scene
